contract.scope: Gate exits caused by loss of the parent signal thesis. No entry signal, sizing, order placement, extra fill or liquidation price is produced.
contract.barClock: A bar is one distinct finalized daily OHLC observation. Do not count polling cycles or duplicate signal publications. Entry fill at UTC open k has age zero; the completed bar k becomes available at open k+1 plus finalization delay and advances age to one. The immediately preceding bar k-1 is pre-entry and cannot advance age or confirmation.
contract.holdingAge: Count completed daily bars after the first actual inventory-acquiring fill. Pending buys have no holding age. Partial exits retain the original entry clock; reset only once inventory is actually zero.
contract.confirmation: While inventory is positive, count consecutive newly finalized post-fill daily observations whose parent thesis is cash. Reset this streak to zero when a newly finalized observation restores the long thesis. Never increment from repeated polling of the same source bar.
contract.btcConfirmationInterpretation: The seven daily observations in the BTC persistence candidate can repeat one unchanged weekly parent state. This is a seven-day persistence/grace test, not seven independent weekly confirmations.
contract.minimumHoldBars: A thesis-loss exit is permitted only if holding age is at least minimumHoldBars AND the consecutive cash-thesis streak is at least thesisBreakConfirmBars. A prior cash streak does not compel exit after the thesis has recovered.
contract.maxHoldBars: When non-null, age at or above this limit requests exit regardless of the current thesis or minimumHoldBars. It is a decision deadline, not a guaranteed last fill date.
contract.priority: Risk or account/data safety exit overrides all holding permissions; maximum age is next; confirmed thesis loss after minimum age is next; otherwise keep existing inventory unchanged.
contract.executionTiming: The decision uses only information finalized by its timestamp and can fill only at a later eligible execution event. No same-bar retrofill, forced stop fill, or reset of the entry clock on a submitted-but-unfilled order.
contract.pendingExit: Holding cannot silently cancel a risk exit or a time-budget exit. Execution owns cancellation/replacement and residual inventory; a partial fill is not a completed episode.
contract.inventory: No additions, pyramiding or averaging down. Holding permission retains current units subject to independent risk reductions; it does not increase an entry budget.
contract.marking: Mark cash plus residual units at a fresh executable bid net of exit costs; when unavailable, report an unavailable mark rather than a synthetic fresh price. Historical daily OHLC marks remain explicitly labeled screening proxies.
contract.boundary: Forced terminal valuations are disclosed separately and never count as natural completed holding episodes.

rationales.btc_hold_immediate_v1: Baseline: preserve immediate response to a lost weekly thesis at the next permitted execution event, with no minimum or time cap.
rationales.btc_hold_weekly_persistence_v1: A one-native-week grace budget reduces responses to a newly weak weekly state; require seven consecutive daily observations of the lost thesis and one week of actual exposure. This tests delayed conviction, while admitting larger reversal losses and repeated-state dependence.
rationales.btc_hold_bounded_thesis_v1: Immediate thesis exit with an 84-day (12-week) exposure budget. Twelve complete weekly opportunities provide a coarse finite review horizon without choosing a time limit from historical trade outcomes. Strong continuing trends may be cut short.
rationales.eth_hold_immediate_v1: Baseline: retain the existing daily thesis response, with no minimum or time cap.
rationales.eth_hold_daily_persistence_v1: Require two finalized daily observations after entry and a two-day consecutive loss of the daily thesis. This tests whether allowing one daily reversal to recover offsets the extra risk and execution delay; two is a minimal confirmation alternative, not an estimated optimum.
rationales.eth_hold_bounded_thesis_v1: Immediate thesis exit with a 40-day exposure budget equal to one full ETH40 lookback. This tests a finite capital commitment tied to the existing signal horizon, not a fitted optimum.

limitations: Different counts follow the parents weekly versus daily signal horizons; no claim that asset labels alone determine optimal holding time.
Cost amortization does not guarantee positive expected return; never defer a mandatory exit merely to recover fees.
All supplied history was previously reused. Chronological partitions are descriptive, not an untouched holdout.
The baseline holding permission is a normalized research component; it does not reproduce every current runtime execution, safety or risk rule.
Parameters frozen before new holding P&L; any implementation correction or contract change requires a disclosed new registration.
